summary.text: Ali Cupper is standing as an independent for Mildura at the 2026 Victorian election. She won the seat in 2018, after losing as Labor's candidate in 2010 and as an independent in 2014, and held it for one term until the Nationals' Jade Benham defeated her in 2022. Before parliament she was a social worker and a family law solicitor, and she returned to Mildura Rural City Council in 2024; the ABC's guide says she is now its mayor.

occupation.text: Family law solicitor and former social worker; principal and director of her own family law firm

prior_roles.role: Deputy Leader (informal coalition with the Reason Party)

prior_roles.organisation: Mildura Rural City Council (Mildura Wetlands Ward)

prior_roles.note: Wikipedia says she was elected deputy mayor in November 2024; the ABC's guide says she is now mayor, so this role is taken to have ended, but no source gives the date.

previous_candidacies.seat: Mildura Rural City Council (Mildura Wetlands Ward)

summary.text: Guy Cooper is the One Nation candidate for Mildura at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says he manages client relationships in agribusiness banking and once worked in a local fruit factory. It also says that earlier in 2026 he was one of three people who sought to be One Nation's candidate at the Farrer by-election in New South Wales. One Nation's page for him refused our requests.

sources.title: Mildura: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Jade Benham won Mildura for the Nationals at the 2022 election, unseating the sitting member Ali Cupper. She was previously mayor of Swan Hill Rural City Council. She was the Nationals' whip in the Assembly until June 2026, when she became shadow minister for water, consumer affairs, and disability, ageing, carers and volunteers. She is recontesting Mildura in 2026.

occupation.text: Owner of a digital communications and marketing business for regional firms; earlier worked in media

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Disability, Ageing, Carers and Volunteers
Shadow Assistant Minister for Regional Development and Agriculture
Nationals Whip in the Legislative Assembly

prior_roles.note: The years are her mayoralty: Wikipedia says she became mayor in November 2021 and took leave in July 2022 to stand for state parliament. Neither source says when she joined the council.

prior_roles.role: Owner of a digital communications and marketing business
prior_roles.note: The Parliament biography gives no years.

prior_roles.role: Role at the Global Digital Media Agency, United Kingdom
prior_roles.note: The Parliament biography gives no years.
The Parliament biography gives no years.

priorities.text: Better health care in regional areas
Backing the region's farmers and food producers
Fixing roads so produce can reach markets and ports

summary.text: Joselyne Ntahomvukiye is the Family First candidate for Mildura at the 2026 Victorian election (the ABC's guide spells her first name Joselyn). Her party page says she came to Australia from Burundi and is now a citizen, and presents her as a Christian whose main causes are human rights and speaking up for vulnerable people and families.

priorities.text: Speaking up for vulnerable people and families
Policies that strengthen families and communities

summary.text: Katie Clements is the Greens candidate for Mildura at the 2026 Victorian election. She teaches at senior high school level and came to Mildura around 25 years ago for work in tourism. She was the Greens candidate for Mildura in 2022 and won a seat on Mildura Rural City Council in 2024.

prior_roles.organisation: Mildura Rural City Council (City Gate Ward)

previous_candidacies.seat: Mildura Rural City Council (City Gate Ward)

priorities.text: Renewable energy and new industries for the Mildura region
Affordable housing, rent caps and other help with living costs

summary.text: Renee Nayef is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Mildura at the 2026 Victorian election. She spent much of her childhood in Robinvale, where her grandparents had settled to pick grapes. A history student, she has helped organise Melbourne's Palestine solidarity movement and has campaigned with refugees for permanent protection.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's results list a Victorian Socialists candidate named Renee Nayef; same name and party, but no source we read says it was her.

priorities.text: Fully funded hospitals and health care in regional areas
Strong rights for farm workers and migrant workers
Public ownership of essential services such as energy and water
More investment in, and justice for, Aboriginal communities in the Mallee

summary.text: Stella Zigouras is the Labor candidate for Mildura at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide describes her as a lawyer who is also an opera singer. She was Labor's candidate for Mildura in 2022, when she received 6.5 per cent of the primary vote. Labor's page for her carried no biography as at early November 2026.
